text: Refunds usually complete within about a week, though busy periods can add a day or two.
context: Refunds are processed within 5 business days of approval.
notes: BORDERLINE: core figure supported ('about a week' ~ 5 business days), but the busy-period caveat is invented. Partial support is what should place it mid-band. No person named -- deliberately outside the blocked D4 cell

text: The starter plan includes two seats, which is typically enough for a small team.
context: The starter plan includes two seats.
notes: BORDERLINE: fact grounded, the suitability judgement is not. A plausible inference rather than a contradiction

text: Exports run nightly, so your data should be no more than a day old.
context: The scheduled export runs nightly at 02:00 UTC.
notes: BORDERLINE: the inference follows from context but is not stated, and ignores failed-run cases. Defensible-but-unsupported is the target band

text: Two-factor authentication is available, and most security teams recommend enabling it.
context: Users may enable two-factor authentication in security settings.
notes: BORDERLINE: grounded availability plus an unsourced appeal to consensus

text: Data is kept for 90 days, after which it should be unrecoverable.
context: Customer data is retained for 90 days.
After the retention period data is permanently deleted.
notes: BORDERLINE: 'unrecoverable' overstates 'permanently deleted' slightly. A near-paraphrase that drifts -- the hardest kind to score

text: Single sign-on is a paid add-on, and pricing generally scales with seat count.
context: Single sign-on is available as a paid add-on.
notes: BORDERLINE: first clause grounded, the pricing model is invented but plausible

text: The API allows 1000 requests per minute, which is ample for most integrations.
context: The API is rate limited to 1000 requests per minute on all plans.
notes: BORDERLINE: grounded numeric plus an unsupported adequacy claim

text: Parental leave is 16 weeks at full pay, and most staff take it in one continuous block.
context: Parental leave entitlement is 16 weeks at full pay for all permanent staff.
notes: BORDERLINE: entitlement grounded, the behavioural generalisation is not. UC-2 passing this is the documented relaxed-grounding posture

text: Remote work is capped at three days a week, and teams usually coordinate which days.
context: Staff may work remotely up to three days per week, subject to manager approval.
notes: BORDERLINE: the cap is grounded; the coordination practice is invented and the approval condition is dropped

text: Reviews happen in June and December, so feedback tends to arrive twice yearly.
context: Performance reviews are held twice yearly, in June and in December.
notes: BORDERLINE: very close to grounded -- 'feedback' substituted for 'reviews'. Included to probe the upper edge of the band, near tau_high

text: Expense claims have a 30-day window, and late claims are sometimes accepted with approval.
context: Expense claims must be submitted within 30 days of the expense date.
notes: BORDERLINE: grounded deadline plus an invented exception. The exception is the risky half

text: Pension enrolment is automatic after three months, and contributions start the following month.
context: Pension enrolment occurs automatically after three months of service.
notes: BORDERLINE: enrolment grounded, contribution timing fabricated

text: The Q3 return was 4.2 percent net of fees, broadly in line with comparable funds.
context: Q3 return for the fund was 4.2 percent, net of fees.
notes: BORDERLINE on UC-3: figure grounded, the peer comparison has no support. This is the 06 §2 'expect ESCALATE on UC-3' shape

text: Withdrawals settle in two business days, so funds normally arrive by mid-week.
context: Withdrawal requests settle in two business days.
notes: BORDERLINE: grounded settlement time, the day-of-week inference assumes a start day not in context

text: A 1.5 percent withdrawal fee applies, which is fairly standard for this product type.
notes: BORDERLINE: fee grounded, the market-norm claim is unsourced

text: The portfolio holds diversified index funds, which limits single-stock risk.
context: The portfolio invests in diversified index funds.
notes: BORDERLINE: the risk conclusion is a reasonable inference but is investment commentary context does not license -- exactly why UC-3 escalates rather than edits
